domain: Public Health Ethics / Constitutional Law / Political Philosophy
topic_summary: Analysis of vaccine mandates as a contested kernel where the same policy instrument (mandatory vaccination) is read through fundamentally incompatible normative frameworks. Public-health-primary readings prioritize collective protection and treat the immunocompromised-exposed as victims of non-compliance. Bodily-autonomy-primary readings prioritize individual consent and treat the unvaccinated-coerced as victims of state overreach. The victim sets do not overlap; the constraints emitted are structurally distinct.

key_entities: Immunocompromised Populations (vulnerable to exposure; benefit from herd immunity)
Mandate Opponents (bodily autonomy framework; vaccine hesitant)
Healthcare Workers (subject to pre-existing occupational mandates; divided on COVID mandates)
State Governments (police power authority; Jacobson precedent)
key_tensions: Collective protection vs individual consent (core ethical conflict)
Functional governance vs political polarization (mandate effectiveness vs backlash)
key_mechanisms: School entry requirements (enforcement via access restriction)
Jacobson v. Massachusetts precedent (constitutional police power)
key_absences: Vaccine injury compensation frameworks (absent from mandate debate framing)
Differential mandate design by transmission risk (blanket vs targeted mandates)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The shared commitment that vaccination policy must balance individual rights against collective welfare, with the mandate as the contested instrument for achieving that balance.
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Constitutional police power (Jacobson precedent) grants states authority to mandate, but interpretive legitimacy contested between public health expertise (epidemiological necessity) and liberal rights theory (consent primacy).

readings.commitment: Collective protection supersedes individual consent when voluntary compliance fails to achieve herd immunity and vulnerable populations face lethal exposure risk.
readings.authority_grounding: Public health expertise; Jacobson precedent; utilitarian harm minimization
readings.expected_structural_delta: Immunocompromised-exposed enter victim set when mandates absent; unvaccinated-coerced not victims (consent subordinated to necessity); high ε from mandate enforcement mechanisms

readings.commitment: Individual consent is inviolable; state cannot compel medical intervention regardless of collective benefit.
readings.authority_grounding: Liberal rights theory; informed consent doctrine; anti-paternalism
readings.expected_structural_delta: Unvaccinated-coerced enter victim set when mandates imposed; immunocompromised-exposed not victims (risk acceptance inherent to liberty); high ε from coercion mechanisms

readings.commitment: Mandates permissible only when disease severity, transmission risk, and vaccine safety meet strict proportionality thresholds; exemptions must be robust.
readings.authority_grounding: Proportionality doctrine; harm principle (Mill); contextual balancing
readings.expected_structural_delta: Both victim sets conditional on disease parameters; ε varies by pathogen (smallpox vs seasonal flu); mandate legitimacy context-dependent rather than categorical

axiom_contradictions.basis: Public-health-primary holds that consent can be legitimately overridden when collective harm exceeds individual autonomy cost. Bodily-autonomy-primary holds that consent is categorically inviolable regardless of collective harm. No single coherent framework can hold both: accepting consent-override-permissibility requires rejecting consent-inviolability, and vice versa.

axes.selection_reason: Core reading with distinct victim set; highest structural delta from bodily_autonomy_primary

axes.structural_delta: Mandate illegitimacy grounded in consent inviolability; unvaccinated-coerced are victims when mandates imposed; immunocompromised-exposed not victims because risk acceptance inherent to liberty.
axes.primary_observable: Mandate enforcement mechanisms (job loss, school exclusion); vaccine hesitancy rates; exemption denial rates
axes.selection_reason: Axiom-contradictory sibling to public_health_primary; non-overlapping victim set

axes.primary_observable: Case fatality rate; R0 value; vaccine adverse event rates; exemption approval rates
axes.selection_reason: Mediating reading that contextualizes the binary; captures policy design space between extremes

axes.selection_reason: Deferred: upstream cultural factor but lower structural distinctiveness than the three readings

omegas.description: Vaccine injury compensation frameworks (VICP in U.S.) absent from mandate debate framing. Does compensation availability alter bodily_autonomy_primary's victim set by providing exit from pure coercion? Or does it function as a Snare (state liability shield masquerading as protection)?

Blanket mandates vs risk-stratified mandates (e.g., healthcare workers only, high-transmission settings only). Does proportionality_reading collapse into public_health_primary when mandates are narrowly targeted? Or does targeting create new victim sets (excluded-from-protection)?

Religious/philosophical exemptions function as political pressure valve (drift_status: partial). Are exemptions a Rope (coordination mechanism preserving pluralism) or a Snare (undermining herd immunity while appearing to respect autonomy)? Exemption prevalence may determine whether proportionality_reading is functional or decorative.

Public_health_primary and bodily_autonomy_primary hold axiom-contradictory commitments. Does proportionality_reading mediate this contradiction or merely defer it? If proportionality thresholds are themselves contested (what CFR justifies mandates?), the reading may collapse back into the binary.
omegas.source: Axiom contradiction declaration between public_health_primary and bodily_autonomy_primary
